# Additional analyses (auto-generated by scripts/extra_analysis.py)

Sample: 17,148 article-country records, 15,730 unique articles. Overall female first-author share: 26.8%.
Gender is the Namsor prediction for the first author, no confidence threshold unless stated.

## 1. Female share by first-author seniority (h-index)

| unit | h 0-2 | h 3-5 | h 6-10 | h 11-20 | h 21-40 | h 41+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| articles | 30.6 (n=1,874) | 32.9 (n=2,928) | 28.2 (n=3,589) | 25.4 (n=3,990) | 20.9 (n=2,691) | 13.4 (n=658) |
| unique first authors | 31.4 (n=1,757) | 33.0 (n=2,510) | 29.1 (n=2,843) | 26.1 (n=2,865) | 22.7 (n=1,730) | 14.1 (n=434) |
| articles, confidence >= 0.6 | 28.4 (n=1,544) | 31.2 (n=2,610) | 26.2 (n=3,241) | 23.1 (n=3,624) | 17.6 (n=2,420) | 9.9 (n=587) |

- Logistic regression (articles, with year and journal controls): odds ratio per unit of log(1 + h-index) = 0.76, p = 1.1e-35.

## 2. Repeat first authorship

| first-author gender | unique authors | mean first-author articles | % with 2+ | % with 3+ | % with 5+ | mean years between first and last (2+ only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| female | 3,409 | 1.24 | 16.0 | 4.5 | 0.6 | 2.7 |
| male | 8,730 | 1.32 | 19.6 | 6.2 | 1.2 | 2.8 |

- Chi-square test for 2+ articles by gender: p = 4.6e-06.
- Female share among unique first authors: 28.1%; among those with one article 29.0%, 2-4 articles 24.6%, 5+ articles 16.9%.
- Authors are matched by exact name, so name variants split one person and common names merge several.

### Female share among new first authors (first appearance in the dataset), by year

| year | 2012 | 2013 | 2014 | 2015 | 2016 | 2017 | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| female % | 25.6 | 23.5 | 26.5 | 29.9 | 26.6 | 29.4 | 29.3 | 31.2 | 29.7 | 28.7 | 28.7 | 30.8 | 30.1 |
| new authors | 770 | 855 | 827 | 795 | 862 | 847 | 819 | 865 | 781 | 727 | 652 | 601 | 1002 |

- Trend among new first authors 2012-2024: +0.42 pp/year, p = 0.005. (2010-2011 are left out because everyone looks new at the start of the data.)

## 3. Team size and collaborators

| first-author gender | mean authors | median authors | % solo-authored | mean of highest co-author h-index | median of highest co-author h-index | % where first author has the highest h-index in the team |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| female | 5.03 | 5 | 3.3 | 45.9 | 40 | 7.2 |
| male | 4.78 | 4 | 5.1 | 45.2 | 39 | 11.6 |

- Mann-Whitney p: team size 2.4e-13; highest co-author h-index 0.0083.
- Solo-authored articles: 728; female share among them 19.1% vs 27.1% for multi-authored.

Citation models on unique articles (log citations; % difference female vs male first author):

| controls | % difference | 95% CI | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| year, journal | +2.9% | -0.5 to +6.5 | 0.091 |
| + team size | +1.8% | -1.6 to +5.3 | 0.3 |
| + team size, highest co-author h-index | +1.1% | -2.3 to +4.5 | 0.53 |
| + team size, highest co-author h-index, first-author h-index | +5.0% | +1.6 to +8.5 | 0.004 |

## 4. Highly cited and uncited articles

Citation rank is computed within journal and publication year, on unique articles from 2010-2022 (later years have had too little time to accumulate citations).

| group | articles | female % | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| all | 13,602 | 26.4 | 25.7-27.2 |
| top 25% | 3,433 | 26.5 | 25.1-28.0 |
| top 10% | 1,399 | 25.7 | 23.5-28.1 |
| top 5% | 715 | 26.2 | 23.1-29.5 |
| top 1% | 173 | 22.5 | 17.0-29.3 |
| bottom 25% | 3,360 | 25.0 | 23.6-26.5 |

- Share of articles reaching the top 10%: female 10.0%, male 10.4% (chi-square p = 0.55).
- Uncited articles: female 0.7%, male 1.3%.
- Baseline female share in this subset: 26.4%.
